citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., Gao, J. (2024). MATHVISTA: EVALUATING MATHEMATICAL REASONING OF FOUNDATION MODELS IN VISUAL CONTEXTS. ICLR.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research)
description: MATHVISTA is a benchmark designed to evaluate the mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA).
name: MATHVISTA
publisher: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research
rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields and expert annotators.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: High inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%. Among the newly collected 736 questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements in the annotated answers. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 for identifying if a problem involves mathematical reasoning.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team, ensuring a consensus was reached on each example. For VQA datasets, annotators labeled examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning using majority voting.
rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets, including 9 math-targeted question answering datasets and 19 VQA datasets. In addition, three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were created by sourcing puzzle test figures from online learning platforms, functional plots, and academic illustrations from papers released on Huggingface.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Existing multimodal datasets, puzzle test figures on online learning platforms, functional plots, and academic illustrations (tables, figures, charts) from online education resources and papers released on Huggingface.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage may have gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations, which lack a unified format and structure.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure a balanced representation in the final compiled benchmark. For VQA datasets, examples were filtered using heuristic rules and then manually labeled, utilizing majority voting and limiting each source dataset to 400 examples.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates. Examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words in the questions were selected.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors will maintain an online evaluation platform and are committed to maintaining the datasets, such as refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
rai:dataUseCases: To facilitate the development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios, and evaluate the research progress of LLMs and LMMs, especially their capabilities in solving rigorous reasoning tasks.

null_reasons.rai:machineAnnotationTools: No machine learning tools were used for annotation (only heuristic rules).
